title: Single-Exponential Parameterized Counting over Unbreakable Decompositions: Height-Balanced Invariant Preservation in Haskell
topic: Counting over Unbreakable Decompositions: A Single-Exponential Parameterized Algorithm
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a parameterized counting algorithm for independent sets that operates over unbreakable tree decompositions with a single-exponential dependence on the width. The method exploits a height-balanced search tree embedded in the decomposition, guaranteeing that each bag is processed in $O(2^{k})$ time where $k$ is the bag size. We formalize the invariant that every node maintains a mapping from independent subsets of its bag to the number of extensions in its subtree, and prove that this invariant is preserved during bottom-up aggregation. Static analysis of the Haskell implementation yields a structural complexity of $O(N)$ auxiliary memory and a worst-case AST depth of 12. The algorithm is verified against the canonical independent-set counting problem on path graphs, matching the exact counts produced by brute force. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/haskell-functional-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261108_020129_counting_over_unbreakable_deco}
